key_insight: Mode connectivity in QML is best understood on the reachable unitary Lie group, where low-loss regions can be path-connected independent of the circuit’s parameterization.
engineering_relevance: This gives a geometry-based way to diagnose and exploit trainability in variational quantum circuits, especially when overparameterization allows Lie-group paths to be realized in parameter space.
method: Define mode connectivity on the reachable unitary Lie group generated by the circuit’s dynamical Lie algebra.
Assume near-minimum connectedness and no critical values in a low-loss band to prove path-connected low-loss sublevel sets.
Use geodesic interpolations between trained unitaries and examine whether they lift to parameter-space paths.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports toy numerical experiments where geodesic interpolation between trained unitaries shows nearly zero loss barriers.
watch_item: The result depends on structural assumptions (near-minimum connectedness and no critical values), so practical circuits may not always satisfy the conditions needed for parameter-space realizability.
paper_title: Lie-Group Mode Connectivity in Quantum Machine Learning from a Dynamical Lie Algebra Perspective
